items.text: Small Ben is top of the weekend, which is the one table he gets to look down on, and it took Enciso poaching a goal at Portman Road to put him there. He still sits 49 behind Marcus overall, a gap he will study the way he studies everything else: from below.

Edward's Friday peaked in the thirteenth minute, when Neco Williams scored, and Return of the Djedi has been a sequel nobody asked for since. Gibbs-White spent the remaining 77 minutes of his 90 contributing very little, and Edward now waits for Saturday with nine players still to come, which is the threat and the warning in one.

Marcus spent Friday night exactly where luck likes him: on the sofa, 19 clear of Justin, with all eleven of his players yet to touch a ball. Everyone else did the work and he leads the weekend's argument by not having started it.

Robert's season is an exercise in watching things leave: Saka's thigh has no return date, the leader has 142 points on him, and his hairline, the only one of the three that was never coming back anyway, is the one holding up best.

Chelsea host Tottenham at 5.30pm BST without Emiliano Martinez, who the Guardian lists with a jaw problem until 21 November, and James is out with a knee until January. items.text: Marcus went to bed on Friday 19 clear of Justin and has spent Saturday finding out what that was worth: 4 points from a day when his own players seemed to have been told the match was elsewhere. A man who relies on luck every week now needs Sunday's to turn up, with six of his eleven still to play and 8 to find. He has the right sort of history for it, and nothing else.

Small Ben had Donnarumma and Ruben at Villa for a full 90 minutes each and got 1 point from both of them, which leaves him 51 behind Justin and, for once, looking up at something taller than himself. Enciso's 10 from Friday is carrying a team that otherwise seems to have been picked by someone standing very far away.

Gabriel gave Robert 16 on Saturday and the rest of his eleven are five men who took part and returned nothing. His hairline and his league position have been receding in step all season, and today Gabriel gave the league position a reprieve and the hairline nothing at all.

Edward had the best day in the league, and the part he will replay is Palmer, who lasted 79 minutes, was sent off, and finished on -1. Jackson hauled 13 and Williams and Leno got 8 each, and still the headline from Return of the Djedi's day is the red card, which tells you how a man who takes the lead at lunchtime ends up third on the night.

Justin's Brobbey is the one name the Guardian's team-news guide lists as doubtful for Sunderland, with a hamstring problem, ahead of the 4.30pm kick-off against Leeds. Sunderland are also without Danso, who is suspended for the match. items.text: Marcus went into the weekend in front and comes out of it 8 behind Justin, after Kostoulas and De Cuyper played the full 90 at Anfield for 3 points between them. A man who relies on luck every week was always going to get a bill, and it came in on a Sunday.

Six of Robert's eleven played and returned nothing, and the one who turned up, Gabriel, scored 17 and made the other ten look like a clerical error. He now sits 139 off the lead, a gap his hairline has been working on for years without getting there. At least the hairline has a plan.

Edward had the biggest gameweek in the league, 56 to Justin's 55, and gained exactly one point on the man he is chasing. Jackson on 13, Truffert on 10, and he still finishes the night third. All that work and the gap barely noticed.
Konsa gave Big Ben 14 and Gross gave him an own goal, so the self-appointed Arsenal man gets to take the first as proof of his ball knowledge and will describe the second as a Brighton problem.

Isak scored the second at Anfield against Brighton, taking him to six Premier League goals this season, more than half of Liverpool's league total and behind only Haaland's nine, the BBC reports. Small Ben has him, and Liverpool host nobody easier next: it is Arsenal.

items.text: Justin started the weekend 19 behind and ends it 8 clear, top of the league on the strength of Ben White and Marcus Tavernier, a right-back and a Bournemouth midfielder on 10 apiece, while Haaland, the one man in his squad anybody else would want, wandered in with 8. It is the leadership style of a man who turns up to the pub last, finds everyone else has already bought a round, and will be telling you about his excellent timing until at least Saturday.

Small Ben left 14 on his bench again, and the pick of it was Zion Suzuki, who made the BBC's team of the week from the dugout while Donnarumma started in goal for 1. Silva sat beside him on 8. A man who cannot find the right eleven out of fifteen with a week's notice is about to get into a boxing ring, and on this evidence his corner should be ready for him to come out for the first round facing the wrong way, assuming anyone can see him over the ropes.

Marcus's best score of the weekend was nine points from Kinsky, who spent it on the bench, which is the only place in the squad that luck could not find him. The man who leans on it every week had it walk out on him, and he went from leading the league to 8 behind Justin on the lowest eleven of the six. Expect a panicked waiver claim on a player with two good games by Tuesday.

Michael Carrick dropped Bruno Fernandes to the bench for the Bournemouth game, and Big Ben, unprompted, had already put him on his own bench. Two men reached the same verdict independently and Bruno returned nothing for either. Meanwhile Trafford sat there on 10 while Kelleher started on 2, so the self-appointed man of ball knowledge picked the wrong goalkeeper and the right midfielder to leave out, entirely by accident.

Robert's bench scored nothing at all, Saka and James and the others, which makes it the only part of the squad that is consistent with the rest of it. He is 139 off the lead and the league still cannot tell whether the plan is patience or whether somebody has forgotten his password. The hairline retreats at a similar pace and with the same lack of resistance.

Ezri Konsa has not just replaced the injured William Saliba at Arsenal, he has Arsenal conceding the fewest goals in the league, and the BBC's piece on him lands the day after he scored his first goal for the club against Everton. It is Big Ben's best outcome of the lot: Konsa was the 14 in his eleven last weekend, and the pair of him and Gabriel, who is Robert's, is now being talked about as the best partnership in the world.

source.title: BBC Sport: No Saliba, no problem - Konsa stepping up for Arsenal

items.text: Justin leads by 8 and has built it on a back line that has been busy making a point of its own: Gvardiol, Vuskovic and Boscagli returned 1 between them last week, and next they get to meet, because Manchester City host Brighton in GW9 and the leader has put his own defenders on both sides of the same corner. He is top of the table and he has arranged to be marking himself.

Robert has Martinez, Estevao and James at Chelsea and Yoro and Sesko at Manchester United, so in GW9 he gets to watch his own team play itself and, going by form, find a way to lose both halves. He is 139 off the lead and has never finished anything he started, ask the pint.

Quantum of Tzolis is the name on Big Ben's team sheet, and the only Tzolis in the whole league is in Marcus's squad, where he returned 0 last week. The man who keeps telling everyone about his ball knowledge named his side after a player he could not be bothered to pick up, and sits 89 behind with an Arsenal pair for company.

Joao Pedro has a thigh injury and no return date, which is the first thing in months that Marcus's luck has not been able to do anything about. He returned 0 last week while healthy, so the injury is mostly a formality, and the man leaning on fortune every week is now 8 behind with a forward line that has taken the hint and gone home.

Arsenal lost to Fleetwood on penalties in the League Cup last night after a 1-1 draw, and the BBC's report lists Bukayo Saka, Christos Tzolis and Noni Madueke as the injured wingers Mikel Arteta had to pick around, which is how a 16-year-old Max Dowman ended up starting and getting sent off. items.text: Edward had the best eleven of the six last week, one point clear of Justin's, with Jackson on 13, Truffert on 10 and Muharemovic on 9, and it moved him nowhere: third on Friday, third tonight, the same distance from the lead as a man gets from a bus he watched leave. The Return of the Djedi has so far been all return and no Jedi.

Small Ben has Rice and Madueke both listed at a 75 percent chance of playing for Arsenal, which is the best odds anyone has offered him all season. The best score in his eleven last week came from an Ipswich player, he is 48 off the top, and his chance of winning the league is still the same size as the man himself, which on current form is a generous reading of the chance.

Saka is in the treatment room, Saka is in Robert's squad, and Saka will still be in Robert's squad when he comes back, because the last transfer Robert made is a story nobody can date and he does not answer when the group chat asks. It is the only squad in the league that can be summed up in a message that went unread. The hairline, at least, has the decency to move on.

Arsenal lost a League Cup tie to Fleetwood on penalties this week, and Big Ben's entire stake in the club is Konsa, who was excellent, and Havertz, who returned 1. Two Arsenal players is a modest return on a lifetime of shouting about them. On Saturday he gets to watch Wirtz play against his own Arsenal, so for once he cannot lose by default.

Bruno Fernandes and Michael Carrick held a private clear-the-air talk at the training ground on Tuesday, BBC Sport reports, after Fernandes criticised the tactics following the 4-1 Champions League loss at Como and was left an unused substitute in the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth. items.text: Marcus put out the lowest-scoring eleven in the league last week, 28, and the best score he owned all week was Kinsky's 9, from the bench, while the keeper he actually started, Becker, got 6. A week ago he led. Tonight he is 8 back, and the man who sells a winger after two good games has just discovered what it feels like to hold the wrong one.

Big Ben started Kelleher, who returned 2, and left Trafford on the bench for 10, which is about what you would expect from a man with this much to say about ball knowledge. The Bruno bail-out never arrived either: Fernandes was left out by Manchester United and then found himself on Big Ben's bench, dropped by the club and by the fan. He is 89 off the lead and on Saturday he gets to be wrong about it live.

Small Ben left 14 points on his bench last week, Silva's 8 among them, while Cunha started and returned 1. There is a fight coming, and this is the best evidence going of how he prepares for one: the right man was in the building all along, in a tracksuit, and never got the call. Foresight, as advertised.

Gabriel gave Robert 17 of his 39 last week and Roefs added 9, so two players did two thirds of the work while the other nine shared 13 and a sincere effort at looking busy. It is the squad of a man whose whole strategy is to touch nothing and answer nobody, and like the hairline, the part that is left is doing everything it can.

Opta's expected points model rates Chelsea the 12th-best side in the Premier League even though they sit fifth, the Guardian reports, because they have scored 6.7 goals more than their chances deserve. It names Pedro Neto, on three league goals and two short of his best for a season, and Morgan Rogers, still ahead of his expected goals but by 1.87 against 3.15 across all of last season, as the ones unlikely to keep it up. Neto is Justin's, Rogers is Big Ben's, and Joao Pedro, whom the piece also lines up, is Marcus's. Chelsea host Manchester United at 12.30pm on Saturday.

source.title: Chelsea's fine finishing has them flying high - but how long can it last?

items.text: Edward spent the day binning Leno, Williams and Horníček, who returned 8 apiece in the best eleven of the week, and took Pickford, Porro and Verbruggen on the strength of nothing anyone has seen yet. The Return of the Djedi has found a way to be kneejerk without any help from Marcus.

Big Ben made five waiver claims today and one of them is McBurnie, of Hull, which is a lot of new names for the man who sells himself as the last word on ball knowledge. He is 89 off the lead and has apparently decided the answer was never at Arsenal after all, only that nobody told the Arsenal fan.

Justin, 8 clear, spent the day adding Odegaard and Gyokeres to a squad that already held Raya and White, so tomorrow's Liverpool v Arsenal puts four of his men on one side of it. Stach and Brobbey went out to make room, and neither will be missed by anyone, least of all the scoreboard. It is a lead protected the traditional way: by owning the whole of one club and then hoping.

The page logged thirteen waiver moves today and none of them were Marcus's, the same Marcus who sold a winger the day after two good games, and who is 8 behind with Tzolis at a 75 percent chance of playing. Either the kneejerk has been put to bed, or the luck has told him to sit tight, and for Marcus it has never been easy to tell which of the two is doing the talking.

Chelsea go into the 12.30 against Manchester United without James (knee, out until January), Joao Pedro (thigh, no return date) and Lacroix (hamstring, no return date), and Martinez is out with a jaw injury until 8 November, the Guardian's predicted lineups report.
